_README: Exceptions for check-table-usage.mjs. Every entry needs a reason.
The gate FAILS only on `twins` — a pair of near-identical tables where one is
written and the other read. readOnly / writeOnly are informational (shown with
--verbose) and listed here so the output stays readable and the intentional
cases are stated once instead of re-argued every run.
KNOWN LIMITATION of the scanner: it matches `.from('t')` chains only. A table
read through a PostgREST nested embed — `products ( combo_items ( ... ) )` —
is invisible to it and will look write-only. That is why combo_items is here.
KNOWN LIMITATION of THIS FILE, added 2026-08-10: every reason below is prose
that nothing checks. `stock_adjustments` sat here for weeks behind a reason
that was false on both of its claims and had never been true, and the effect
was to silence the one gate built to catch exactly that table's shape (B6).
An exception is a claim about the code, and an unverified claim in a file
whose whole job is suppressing warnings is the most expensive kind.
So: re-derive a reason before trusting it, and prefer a reason a reader can
check in one grep ('written by RPC apply_credit_transaction') over one they

readOnly.reason: Reference data. Seeded by migration and by 59_backfill_default_role_permissions. The app never writes it.
Reference data. Rows are created in the admin portal by hand / by migration, never by application code.
Written exclusively by the apply_credit_transaction RPC, which the scanner cannot see. Reading it in credit.ts is correct.

FINDING, NOT AN EXCEPTION — register A49. Left listed so the gate output stays readable, but the entry below is the truth and it is not a justification. Read at reports.ts:286 only. Written NOWHERE: not apps/server, not apps/dashboard, not apps/desktop, not any migration, not any RPC. So the 'restocked' and 'written_off' columns of the stock-movement report are permanently zero, and the report says nothing was ever restocked or written off. This entry PREVIOUSLY read 'Written by the till via /api/sync/push, which resolves the table name dynamically' — both halves were false and had never been true: /api/sync/push writes exactly four hardcoded tables (business_days, shifts, float_transactions, expenses) and stock_adjustments appears in neither SYNC_DIRECTION nor the till's localDb.ts. Adjustments are actually recorded in stock_movements (stockEffects.ts:378, orders.ts:1097, fueltanks.ts:194, branches.ts:162). Fix needs a product decision — point the report at stock_movements, or drop the table and the report section. Do not remove this note to make the output tidy.
